findings.reason: without an amendment the node in the pass branch cannot construct a negative control that fires, and a node choosing the prompt route can pass its gate with a control that never fails.
findings.text: the Negative control removes "the fix the node chose … (the startup allowance, the faster start or the prompt route, whichever it is)", but the Deliverable as changed says the prompt instruction ships either way and only a startup change is withheld when the unfixed session passes, so the prompt route is no longer a fix the node chooses — and the test it must falsify asserts that a seeded launch "carries the instruction", which survives removal of only the search-route clause, so the one fix now always shipped is the one the control cannot show firing, while in the pass branch the control names no fix at all

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — the §10 heading exists at docs/plans/workers-spend-fewer-tokens-per-landed-node.html:115, §4 and §5 headings exist, and the cited run `r-20261111T130138944743-ab2-clive-anchored-a-gate-halts-s4`, the `clive` tool and the `clive-anchored` arm label all resolve as the prior review confirmed against this same section.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — the negative control still names "the prompt route" as a fix the node may have "chosen", while the changed deliverable now makes the prompt instruction ship unconditionally, so that control has no clause it can remove to make the test fail and, in the branch where the unfixed session passes, names no fix at all.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the experiment's session-start records are kept as gate logs and the transcript "beside the record", which are crew run-directory records a later reader opens; no session scratchpad or node-local temporary path is named as the store.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the section names mechanisms and an arm label, and carries no plan labels, ticket numbers, version tags or changelog prose into code.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the Why's hedged root cause now matches its evidence (the server `pending` at session start, the prompt naming no tool, and a `ToolSearch` count without membership), the endpoint is checkable through the headless session records and the closing run, and item (2)'s "launch step that seeds the anchored server" states the condition under which a run gets the instruction rather than a step to implement.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — the section has one goal (a Claude-dialect anchored worker is offered the tool and told to use it); the two changes are two parts of that one endpoint.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §8's `plan-section-depends-on` entry names s10, and §10's own upstreams (§4's seeding step, §5's prompt pattern) are both `done`, so no ordering edge is missing; the absent s10 entry in the depends-on map was declined earlier and orders nothing today.
